class.name: LRTVolume3D
class.brief_description: Configures a local LRT diffuse global illumination volume.
class.description: Activation follows [method Node3D.is_visible_in_tree], including ancestor visibility. There is no global or per-volume Enabled switch. Hidden volumes do not inject or propagate lighting, submit geometry rebuilds, blend into surfaces, or supply boundary lighting. Their baked data and per-volume CPU/GPU caches are retained. In-flight geometry jobs may finish, but publication and further submissions pause until shown. On showing, pending geometry changes are processed before the volume supplies lighting again. Remove or free the node to release its runtime caches. Activation is not tied to camera frustum or occlusion culling. Defines a regular probe grid in local space. Translation, rotation and positive uniform scale are supported. The volume is centered on the node origin and edited through [member size], like [VoxelGI]. Drag the six face handles to resize a face, or hold [kbd]Alt[/kbd] to resize symmetrically about the center. Grid snapping, cancel and undo use the standard 3D editor behavior. Probe positions start at -size / 2 and advance by [member probe_spacing]; the final probe on each axis may lie just beyond the bounds to cover a partial cell. Select this node and use [b]Bake LRT Volume[/b] in the 3D toolbar, or call [method bake], to bake visible, unowned Static GI mesh instances in the volume and its probe neighborhood, together with all owned Details. Inside states use the absolute generalized winding number greater than 0.5, allowing open and nonmanifold meshes to contribute locally enclosed regions. Closed manifolds use an equivalent accelerated ray query. Single sheets do not define a solid interior. Dynamic and Disabled GI instances are excluded from the static bake. When this volume is visible in the scene tree, CPU workers rebuild 8×8×8-probe trunks affected by participating Dynamic GI instances and external Static GI instances with [LRTGeometryBinding] metadata, configured through Global Illumination > LRT in the Inspector. Instance movement, visibility, GI mode, bindings and baked-resource changes invalidate affected trunks. The global rendering/global_illumination/lrt/geometry_trunks_per_frame budget limits submissions across all volumes. Ready trunks are packed on workers and published independently through [signal geometry_updated], without waiting for the full dirty region. Old and new instance bounds are marked separately and deduplicated. A bounded in-flight batch finishes while pending changes are coalesced in FIFO order; in-flight work is never exposed through [method get_geometry_trunk]. Completed trunks are queued to the rendering thread as GPU scatter uploads. Each shared Edge has one canonical owner that updates both endpoints; uploads from its non-owning endpoint cannot overwrite it. Replacing a static baseline first recomposes its dynamic snapshot on a worker and publishes the complete result together, while retaining the previous published CPU/GPU cache during computation. Each changed probe updates its packed geometry and fixed emission. Probes outside solids both before and after the update preserve both L/A propagation histories and continue converging under the new geometry. Inside probes clear both histories; probes newly exposed from Inside initialize both histories to L=0, A=LocalVis. Full volume resets initialize all histories. Geometry uploads do not overwrite untouched probes; normal propagation continues to update them. Removing the volume or blocking CPU geometry releases its GPU buffers; hiding it retains them. GPU lighting and surface sampling require the Forward+ renderer; unsupported renderers report a blocked GPU status rather than substituting another GI path. After shadow rendering, each world alternates between an A update and an L update. An A update propagates global visibility; an L update injects direct light, visible sky and fixed emission as S=T(Ddirect+B)+J, then propagates L. Both use 26 neighbors, shared Edge masks, decoded LocalVis/LTM and independently indexed FP32 ping-pong histories. Each iteration directly writes the newly computed result; surface sampling reads the latest completed A and L every view. Directional, Omni and Spot lights with Static or Dynamic bake mode are collected from the world. Injection uses linear, unexposed colors, indirect energy, range/cone attenuation and current shadow maps. Shadowed positional lights without available current shadow data are not injected; directional lights outside shadow coverage use propagated A. Environment ambient source, color, energy, sky contribution and sky rotation produce world-space Sky SH. Each world updates once per runtime frame using the first rendered view of that world. rendering/global_illumination/lrt/propagation_iterations controls the iteration count for the active field per world update. Inside probes remain zero. Each iteration reads only the previous buffer; barriers separate dependent passes. Volumes update from lower to higher priority, with scene-tree order as the tie-breaker. Each parent completes before its Details; Details read only their parent. Out-of-grid neighbors sample the highest-priority ready lower-priority volume covering that world position and rotate SH into the current volume. Boundary interpolation includes Inside zero states and ignores display intensity and coverage. With no supplier, boundaries are open (A=SH_ONE, L=0). [b]Development status:[/b] Forward+ direct Probe sampling is available when rendering/global_illumination/lrt/screen_gather_enabled is false. Surface sampling offsets the lookup position along the world-space unit surface normal by the receiving instance's [member LRTGeometryBinding.surface_normal_bias], or rendering/global_illumination/lrt/surface_normal_bias (default 0.1 meters) when inherited. The offset is independent of probe spacing and node scale. Sampling interpolates eight Probes after excluding Inside samples, uses identical normalized weights for L and A, and does not query Edge visibility. It reconstructs indirect irradiance/pi and blends with original ambient lighting before material color and AO. Volume coverage and edge blending use the original, unshifted surface position. With a positive valid trilinear weight sum, coverage depends only on volume edge blending and is not attenuated by the weight sum. With no valid samples, the volume is skipped. Losing the last valid contribution can cause an abrupt transition to lower-priority volumes or original ambient lighting. Excessive bias can lose contact detail or cross narrow geometry. With no active ready volume, surfaces use original ambient lighting. With rendering/global_illumination/lrt/screen_gather_enabled enabled, each viewport requests a normal/depth prepass and builds a premultiplied HDR lighting/coverage cache at scale 1, 0.5 or 0.25, with representative position/normal guides and a shared SurfaceProfile ID. Transparent passes and unmatched surfaces use direct Probe sampling. SurfaceProfile shares the exact normal bias and receiver scope across matching instances. Static instances receive only public LRTVolume3D groups plus their own LRTGI group, if any; Dynamic and Disabled instances receive all covering groups. Details inherit their parent group identity. The normal/depth prepass writes an R32_UINT profile ID, with a reserved suppression value for valid Lightmap, Lightmap Capture or VoxelGI. SDFGI does not suppress LRT: eligible LRT samples blend over the original indirect diffuse lighting, including SDFGI, using their effective coverage. Full coverage replaces it, including valid black samples; edges and invalid or uncovered samples retain the corresponding original lighting. Native specular reflections and LRT boundary propagation are unchanged. MSAA resolve selects the integer ID from the same sample as depth and normal. Gather is reused only when profile IDs match and the existing position/normal checks pass; other surfaces use direct sampling with their own profile. Mode, ownership and bias changes apply without baking. View caches encode camera exposure once before FP16 storage to preserve HDR range; world propagation and boundary inputs remain unexposed. Sky uses an additional unexposed material output without changing the original Godot sky cache. Display Advanced provides ten LRT views: gathered indirect lighting, direct Probe sampling, propagated Probe lighting, local visibility, global visibility, Edge visibility, static LTM, Color SDF, Trunk updates and Volume Blending. Selecting a group observes the parent and all its Details; selecting a Detail observes only it. GeometryInstance3D selection does not filter diagnostics. Color SDF shows the observed grids' actual contributors, not the selected instance's resource. Diagnostics and legends are shown directly in the viewport. Material support is the same as [LRTGeometryBinding].

method.name: inspect_probe
method.description: Reconstructs the selected probe's 26 current geometry queries for diagnostics. Returns point, coordinate, samples and the published cache revision when available. Each sample reports position, hit, albedo, emission and the shared four-bit edge_mask; supplied boundary neighbors also report boundary_volume, boundary_index and boundary_direction_in_source. Static queries build a BVH of current scene geometry; dynamic queries use current instance snapshots. These queries may differ from the published cache during pending rebuilds or after unbaked static edits. This is a synchronous diagnostic operation, not a normal per-frame rendering API.

method.name: bake
method.description: Starts an explicit asynchronous static bake using the same core in the editor and at runtime. Searches [param from_node], or the current scene (edited scene in the editor) when null. Scene input is captured in bounded main-thread steps; material readback, geometry, Probe and Edge generation execute asynchronously. Successful completion atomically assigns the finished [member bake_data]; failure or cancellation preserves the previous result. No file is required or saved. Use the returned [LRTBakeTask] for progress, cancellation, resource issues and completion. Saving through [ResourceSaver] is a separate operation.

method.name: get_bounds
method.description: Returns the local-space coverage AABB, centered on the node origin with dimensions [member size].

method.name: get_geometry_status
method.description: Returns CPU geometry scheduling diagnostics. state is disabled, pending, updating, ready, failed or blocked. A failed CPU task reports its error and retains the last valid published cache, when ready is true; it does not retry every frame. Hide and show the volume or assign different bake_data to retry. ready indicates a published dynamic snapshot is available, which may be older than a currently computing batch. Active states include revision, pending_trunks, computing_trunks, cached_trunks, last_submitted_trunks, last_changed_trunks, cpu_task_usec (cumulative rebuild and packing worker time), published_trunks (local trunk publications), last_result_age_usec (snapshot-to-CPU-publication age, including index/worker queueing but excluding later render-thread/GPU delay) and error. frame_submitted_trunks counts submissions across all volumes during the current runtime frame. A blocked volume cannot supply geometry. The gpu subdictionary reports pending, ready or blocked, with the last render-thread-committed revision, grid_size, updated_probes, allocated_bytes and optional error. A ready GPU revision means its commands precede subsequent render work, not that the GPU has finished execution. After propagation, gpu also includes propagation_frame (runtime frame of the last dispatch), propagation_steps (total A and L passes since the full baseline reset), propagation_iterations, propagation_phase (last render-thread-submitted phase) and visibility_history_index/light_history_index (latest submitted buffer for each field). injected_lights reports the number of collected light inputs and surface_sampling indicates that the direct-sampling buffers were prepared. cpu_submit_usec measures per-volume propagation/injection command submission. gpu_usec and gpu_timing_frame report delayed GPU timestamp measurements for the volume update, including final sampling publication, not whole-frame overhead. a_gpu_usec, inject_gpu_usec and l_gpu_usec separate the visibility, injection and light phases; a skipped phase is zero for gpu_timing_frame. gpu_timing_phase identifies that delayed GPU timing frame and is distinct from propagation_phase. world_gpu_timings contains update_gpu_usec (the whole world update, including sky projection, metadata and all volume updates), sky_gpu_usec (sky SH projection, included in update_gpu_usec) and sun_gpu_usec (additional LRT solar shadow draws); world_cpu_submit_usec measures world-update command submission. These world fields are repeated on each volume and must only be counted once per world. upload_gpu_usec and scatter_gpu_usec report geometry upload and its scatter phase, summed across this volume's submissions in upload_timing_frame; the scatter phase is included in the upload total. Upload timings are separate from world and volume lighting updates. All GPU timings use the same native Visual Profiler timestamp stream, grouped by stable world, volume and render-buffer IDs. Parent and child timings must not be added together. They exclude Gather, the extra sky-material output, surface-profile prepass/resolve and material sampling overhead; whole-LRT incremental cost requires a same-view LRT-on/off measurement. gather_size, gather_bytes, gather_cpu_usec, gather_gpu_usec and gather_timing_frame describe the latest rendered view. surface_profiles and surface_profile_bytes report the shared exact configuration count and storage. sampling_bytes reports world-shared profiles/flags/history/metadata storage, sky_cache_bytes reports the optional unexposed sky cache, and debug_bytes reports optional direct-light diagnostics. CPU worker time is cumulative. Normal status queries do not synchronize or read back the GPU. GPU failures discard the cache and require a full baseline reset (for example, reassign bake_data or hide and show the volume).

method.name: get_geometry_gpu_trunk
method.description: Synchronously reads one trunk back from the GPU for diagnostics. This stalls rendering and must not be used in normal per-frame rendering. Returns coordinate, origin, size, revision, ltm, local_vis, edge_masks, emission (12 FP32 coefficients per probe, including zeros when absent), light_0/light_1 (12 FP32 coefficients per probe) and visibility_0/visibility_1 (4 FP32 coefficients per probe). Also returns source (12 FP32 S coefficients per probe, empty before light injection), sky (12 world-space Sky SH coefficients when available), visibility_history_index, light_history_index, propagation_frame and propagation_steps; use each field's index to select its latest submitted state. The other history buffer can contain the preceding iteration. Internally each history uses four contiguous FP32 SH4 planes (R, G, B, A), one entry per probe in each plane. Returned diagnostic arrays remain probe-major. Returns an error field when GPU data is unavailable or the coordinate is invalid. Call on the main thread. GPU storage uses 72 bytes of aligned packed geometry, 48 bytes of fixed emission, 48 bytes of injected source S and two 64-byte L/A histories per probe (296 bytes total). Direct surface sampling additionally maintains 68 bytes per probe in world-shared GPU flags/final-history storage. The last iteration publishes its updated field, the other field's latest history and current flags to the sampling buffer. A and L have independent history indices and each phase writes only its own field. Sampling storage also includes 144 bytes per volume of metadata, a 64-byte metadata header, 16 bytes per distinct SurfaceProfile and 48 bytes of Sky SH. allocated_bytes reports only the per-volume propagation buffers, excluding world-shared sampling buffers, transient light inputs/staging, shaders and driver allocation overhead. Optional static-LTM diagnostics use another 72 bytes per probe. View caches use an R32_UINT SurfaceProfile ID per full-resolution pixel (and a matching multisample attachment when MSAA is enabled). Gather uses 28 bytes per low-resolution pixel: FP16 lighting/coverage, FP32 position/normal guide and R32_UINT representative profile ID. The optional unexposed Sky material cache uses FP32 RGB(A) with three mip levels, preserving values beyond FP16 range.

method.name: get_geometry_trunk
method.description: Returns the last published CPU geometry for a zero-based trunk coordinate. Fields are coordinate, origin (probe grid coordinate), size (at most 8 per axis), ltm, local_vis, edge_masks, emission, instances (instance IDs in stable order), and revision. Channel layouts match [LocalLRTVolumeData], with x-fastest samples within the trunk. Untouched trunks use the static bake. Requires a ready, unblocked published cache; never returns worker-owned in-flight data. During a same-layout static replacement it continues returning the previous published cache until the complete replacement is ready. Returned arrays are independent copy-on-write values.

method.name: get_grid_size
method.description: Returns ceil(size / probe_spacing) + 1 on each axis, including the boundary probes.

members.member: Static geometry cache for this volume. Only an explicit successful bake replaces this baseline. Source movement, visibility, removal, reparenting or unloading never invalidates existing static data. A changed grid layout requires rebaking.

Width of the final display blend at the volume boundary, measured in world-space meters, independent of probe spacing and node scale. Zero disables the transition. This only affects display and requires no bake.
Nonnegative display intensity, applied before volume blending, not to propagated boundary light.
Lower-priority volumes supply boundary lighting to higher-priority volumes. Higher priority also takes precedence in final blending.
Positive probe spacing in local meters. A carriage typically uses 0.25 meters.
Local-space volume dimensions in meters, centered on the node origin. All dimensions must be positive. Use the node transform to position and rotate the volume.

signal.name: geometry_updated
signal.description: Emitted on the main thread after publishing ready CPU geometry results. Read changed trunks with [method get_geometry_trunk]. When reset is true, a complete initial, layout-reset or static replacement cache, already composed with its dynamic snapshot, is available. The flag describes replacement of CPU geometry, not resetting air-probe lighting: a same-layout static replacement preserves those histories. Shared Edge masks at both endpoints change in the same GPU dispatch, even if the adjacent trunk has not completed. Further instance changes during worker execution are retained for a later batch. The corresponding GPU scatter upload and required history initialization for layout changes or Inside-transition probes have been queued before this signal. Light injection and propagation happen later during Forward+ rendering, not during this notification. CPU notification does not wait for the rendering thread or GPU; compare the gpu revision in [method get_geometry_status] when inspecting upload progress.
